claim: Undifferentiated human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) contain only six TAFs (TAFs 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 11).
source_text: Here we find, unexpectedly, that undifferentiated human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) contain only six TAFs (TAFs 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 11)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by immunoblot analysis and qRT-PCR data presented in Figure 1A and 1B showing TAF levels in H9 hESCs compared to HeLa cells.

claim: Following differentiation of hESCs, all TAFs are expressed.
source_text: whereas following differentiation all TAFs are expressed
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by immunoblot data in Figure 1D showing TAF expression after retinoic acid-induced differentiation.

claim: Most active genes in hESCs are bound by only TAFs 3 and 5 along with TBP.
source_text: most active genes are bound by only TAFs 3 and 5 along with TBP
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by directed and global chromatin immunoprecipitation analyses presented in Figures 3, 4, 6, and 7.

claim: The remaining active genes in hESCs are bound by TBP and all six hESC TAFs.
source_text: whereas the remaining active genes are bound by TBP and all six hESC TAFs
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by ChIP and ChIP-chip data showing two classes of genes with different TAF occupancy patterns.

claim: hESCs contain a previously undescribed complex comprising TAFs 2, 6, 7, 11 and TBP.
source_text: Consistent with these results, hESCs contain a previously undescribed complex comprising TAFs 2, 6, 7, 11 and TBP.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by sucrose gradient sedimentation and co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Depleting TAFs that are present in hESCs results in misregulated expression of pluripotency genes and induction of differentiation.
source_text: Altering the composition of hESC TAFs, either by depleting TAFs that are present or ectopically expressing TAFs that are absent, results in misregulated expression of pluripotency genes and induction of differentiation.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments and alkaline phosphatase staining shown in Figures 5 and 8.

claim: Ectopically expressing TAFs that are absent in hESCs results in misregulated expression of pluripotency genes and induction of differentiation.
source_text: Altering the composition of hESC TAFs, either by depleting TAFs that are present or ectopically expressing TAFs that are absent, results in misregulated expression of pluripotency genes and induction of differentiation.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by ectopic TAF expression experiments shown in Figure 8D-I.

claim: The selective expression and use of TAFs underlies the ability of hESCs to self-renew.
source_text: Thus, the selective expression and use of TAFs underlies the ability of hESCs to self-renew.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the combined data showing that altering TAF composition leads to differentiation and loss of pluripotency markers.
